$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under scripts/ or src/ imports this file.
tranche: A3 — a real RateLimiter, and the providers ProviderProbeCache
purpose: A3 turns `packages/adapters/redis-ratelimit` from a generated placeholder
into a real adapter, and gives `providers`' `ProviderProbeCache` its first
implementation as a FOURTH port on `packages/adapters/redis-cache`.
THE ENTRIES THIS LEDGER EXISTS FOR ARE M06 AND M07. They mutate the ORACLE —
`internal-packages/tenancy-database/src/auth.ts`, byte-identical to
origin/main — and watch this branch's differential go red. Without them,
'the hot limiter's windows are the canonical store's windows' would be an
argument about a table this tranche wrote. `oracle-source.ts` LIFTS four
expressions and three literals out of that file and EVALUATES them, so
nothing on the oracle's side of the comparison is written here.
M09 IS A 2x2 RATHER THAN A MUTATION, and it is the only shape that could
settle the claim it is about. `evictionPattern` derives its SCAN pattern from
`domain/health.ts`'s own key builder instead of writing the layout out again.
Mutating the adapter alone kills for the wrong reason; what proves the
derivation load-bearing is moving the DOMAIN's layout and observing that the
derived pattern follows it (green) while a hand-written one does not (red).
M04 IS RECORDED WITH THE STEP THAT MADE IT FIRE, because the first run was
a FALSE GREEN. A context edit does not reach an adapter's suite until
`pnpm build:v1` re-emits the context's `dist/`, which the workspace `exports`
map points at. Anyone re-running this ledger must build between applying a
mutation in `packages/contexts/**` and running the command.
WHAT IS NOT HERE. The atomicity claim — 'two processes consuming the last
token must not both succeed' — is declared UNFALSIFIABLE ON THIS MACHINE
below, with the reason and the suite that would settle it. A Map in one
process cannot exhibit the race, and no unit mutation can kill a case that
does not run.
procedure: PROVE GREEN FIRST. The unmutated tree was run green before and after every
`pnpm --filter @platos/core-api test`. An entry whose suite was already red
proves nothing, and a 'kill' with no named failing line is VACUOUS.
For one entry: apply `to` to `file`, run `command` (running `pnpm build:v1`
`internal-packages/**` — see M04), confirm the NAMED case in `kills` appears
and the process exits non-zero. Then revert and confirm exit 0. Every `kills`
line below was SEEN, on this branch, at the commit that introduces this file.
`file` is REPOSITORY-relative. AFTER any entry that touches the oracle, run
confirm it is EMPTY. That file is the frozen oracle; a tranche that left it
edited would have edited the thing it is measured against.

mutations.name: M01 the bucket key forgets which window it is counting
mutations.why: The window start is IN the key, which is what makes a rolled-over window a different counter with no sweeper and no TTL dependence. Drop it and every window for one identifier shares one counter forever.
kills: × the window rolls over because the KEY changes, not because a TTL fired > addresses a DIFFERENT key the instant the window ends
→ expected 'platos:identity:ratelimit:LOGIN:01234…' not to be 'platos:identity:ratelimit:LOGIN:01234…'
× the window rolls over because the KEY changes, not because a TTL fired > starts the next window's counter at one, with the clock ADVANCED and never read
→ expected 8 to be 1
× this adapter's window is the oracle's window > gives two instants ONE key exactly when the oracle gives them one row
→ LOGIN 2026-03-04T10:17:00.000Z vs 2026-03-04T10:18:00.000Z: expected true to be false
mutations.note: The third kill is the ORACLE's: the equivalence relation the adapter's key induces stopped matching the one the canonical store's unique index induces.

mutations.name: M02 the reported count is off by one
mutations.why: The port says the returned count includes the current request, which is why a caller compares with `>` and a policy of ten admits the tenth. Off by one and a policy of ten admits eleven.
kills: × the bucket a consumption folds into > reports the count the server returned, including this request
→ expected [ +0, 1, 2, 3 ] to deeply equal [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ]
× the request the oracle refuses is the request this adapter's count identifies > refuses the (limit + 1)th and no earlier one, for all three policies
→ LOGIN: expected [ 12 ] to deeply equal [ 11, 12 ]
mutations.note: The second kill is the ORACLE's own comparison, evaluated from its source text, applied to this adapter's count. It is the strongest single line of evidence in this ledger.

mutations.name: M03 a dead Redis fails OPEN by inventing a bucket
mutations.guards: packages/adapters/redis-ratelimit/src/rate-limiter.ts — the catch that refuses instead of fabricating
mutations.why: A synthesised `requestCount: 1` is indistinguishable from a real first request of a window: `decide()` allows it, no safety event is recorded, and the outage is invisible. This is the live security hole the tranche brief names.
kills: × a Redis that is gone > refuses with its own code rather than throwing
→ expected true to be false
× a Redis that is gone > FAILS CLOSED: it never invents a bucket a caller could mistake for a quiet window
→ expected true to be false
× a Redis that is gone > carries the driver's MESSAGE and never the connection URL
→ expected true to be false

mutations.name: M04 the limiter refuses under the identity store's code
mutations.guards: packages/contexts/identity-access/domain/errors.ts — RATE_LIMITER_UNAVAILABLE as a code of its own
mutations.why: `consume-rate-limit.ts` copies `consumed.error.code` verbatim into the `identity.rate_limit.degraded` safety event. Two guards under one code cannot be told apart, so an operator reading that event could not say whether Redis or PostgreSQL had gone.
kills: × a Redis that is gone > refuses with its own code rather than throwing
→ expected 'IDENTITY_STORE_UNAVAILABLE' to be 'RATE_LIMITER_UNAVAILABLE'
mutations.note: FALSE GREEN ON THE FIRST RUN, recorded because it is a trap for the next agent: without `pnpm build:v1` the adapter's suite resolves the context through its published `dist/` and the mutation is invisible. 19/19 passed. After the build it kills.

mutations.name: M05 the counter is written with a lifetime of zero
mutations.why: Redis treats `PEXPIRE key 0` as a DEL, so a caller whose `at` sat on or past the boundary would silently reset a live window — a rate limiter that resets itself on request.
kills: × the lifetime the counter is written with > is never zero or negative, because PEXPIRE 0 is a DELETE
→ expected +0 to be 1

mutations.name: M09 the eviction pattern is written out instead of derived — a 2x2
mutations.guards: packages/adapters/redis-cache/src/provider-probe-cache.ts — `evictionPattern` deriving the layout from the domain's own builder
mutations.why: A hand-written `provider-health/<id>/*` agrees with the domain until somebody changes the domain, and then eviction silently stops matching and a rotated credential's verdict survives its whole freshness window. A single mutation cannot show that; the 2x2 can.
matrix: derived pattern + live layout          -> 68 passed  (the unmutated tree)
hand-written pattern + live layout     -> 1 failed   (it drops the model-list half; the WEAK kill)
hand-written pattern + MOVED layout    -> 3 failed   (the layouts diverge; the REAL kill)
derived pattern + MOVED layout         -> 68 passed  (the derivation follows: THE CONTROL)
kills: × a key rotated because it leaked must stop answering healthy > EVICTS the pre-rotation verdict, so nothing still holding the old fingerprint can read it
→ expected 2 to be +0
× a key rotated because it leaked must stop answering healthy > evicts ONLY that provider, so one rotation does not re-probe every other
→ expected [ …(2) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]
× the eviction pattern is DERIVED from the domain's key builder > matches every fingerprint under one provider and nothing under another
→ expected 'platos:providers:probe:provider-healt…' to be 'platos:providers:probe:probe/health/o…'
mutations.control: The fourth row of the matrix is the load-bearing one: with the layout moved to `probe/health/${provider}/...` and the DERIVED pattern restored, all 68 cases pass. `packages/contexts/providers/domain/health.ts` was restored afterwards and `git diff` was empty for it.

mutations.name: M10 an empty model list is treated as a miss
mutations.why: The port is explicit that an empty array is a STORED ANSWER: caching the empty result of a failed fetch briefly is what stops a broken upstream being called once per page load.
mutations.from: if (!Array.isArray(parsed) || parsed.some((entry) => typeof entry !== "string")) return null;
mutations.to: if (!Array.isArray(parsed) || parsed.length === 0 || parsed.some((entry) => typeof entry !== "string")) return null;
kills: × what a stored value is when it comes back > keeps an EMPTY model list as an answer, because the port says it is one
→ expected { ok: true, value: null } to deeply equal { ok: true, value: [] }

mutations.name: M11 the stored instant comes back as a string
mutations.why: `isFresh` does arithmetic on `checkedAt`. A string would make every freshness comparison NaN-false, so every cached verdict would read as stale and every page load would re-probe — a cache that silently does nothing.
mutations.to: return parsed as unknown as ProviderHealthReport;
kills: × what a stored value is when it comes back > round-trips a report, with its instant still an instant
→ expected { provider: 'openai', …(6) } to deeply equal { provider: 'openai', …(6) }

declared.name: D01 THE ATOMICITY OF THE LAST TOKEN — unfalsifiable on this machine, and named
declared.claim: Two processes consuming the last token of a window must not both succeed. `client.ts` does INCR and the expiry decision in ONE Lua script, so of two callers arriving at a counter of nine one is handed ten and the other eleven.
declared.why-not-mutated: The only suite that can exhibit the race is `packages/adapters/redis-ratelimit/src/ratelimit.integration.test.ts`, which needs a real Redis in a container. Docker is quit on the laptop by standing instruction, and this agent's worktree isolation REFUSED the mutating git-over-ssh calls that put a commit on the Mac mini — `ssh mini 'git -C ~/work/platos-oss fetch …'` is declined because the remote command's text cannot be shown not to be a git operation on another checkout. Routing around that guard was refused.
declared.measured-instead: The suite compiles (it is inside `pnpm build:v1`, which passes) and FAILS LOCALLY with `Error: Could not find a working container runtime strategy`, which is the correct behaviour for a suite reaching for an absent daemon. It is UNVERIFIED, not passing.
declared.what-would-settle-it: On a host with a daemon: `pnpm --filter @platos/adapter-redis-ratelimit exec vitest run src/ratelimit.integration.test.ts`. The mutation that would kill it is replacing the Lua script in `client.ts` with a client-side `GET` then `SET`, at which point 'hands 32 simultaneous consumers 32 DISTINCT counts' must go red. A sequential loop cannot tell the two implementations apart, which is why no unit entry above claims it.

declared.name: D02 `SET … PXAT` on a real server — unfalsifiable on this machine, and named
declared.claim: `RedisConnection.writeUntil` honours an ABSOLUTE instant, so the probe cache needs no clock; an instant already past stores nothing rather than storing an immortal key.
declared.why-not-mutated: Same reason as D01: `packages/adapters/redis-cache/src/provider-probe.integration.test.ts` needs a container. The unit suite proves the instant crosses the seam unchanged (`writes the domain's INSTANT and computes no lifetime of its own`) and can prove nothing about what Redis does with it.
declared.measured-instead: Compiles; excluded from the laptop run by the package's own `test` script; UNVERIFIED.
declared.what-would-settle-it: `pnpm --filter @platos/adapter-redis-cache exec vitest run src/provider-probe.integration.test.ts` on a host with a daemon. `PXAT` is Redis 6.2+ and the harness runs `redis:7-alpine`.

declared.name: D03 THE COMPOSED SYSTEM STILL FAILS OPEN — a measured divergence from the brief, not an oversight
declared.claim: This ADAPTER fails closed (M03 pins it). The SYSTEM does not: `packages/contexts/identity-access/domain/rate-limit.ts` declares `LIMITER_UNAVAILABLE_POLICY = "allow"`, and `consume-rate-limit.ts` admits the request as `degraded` and records a safety event.
declared.why-not-changed: It is the ORACLE's behaviour — `apps/agent/src/auth/rate-limit.guard.ts` catches a failed pipeline with `// Redis down -> fail open (availability over rate limiting).` and returns `true`. Flipping the constant is a behaviour change to a live authentication path, it is a DOMAIN edit rather than an adapter one, and it would be invisible in a diff of the two adapter directories this tranche is scoped to.
declared.already-pinned: `packages/contexts/identity-access/domain/rate-limit.test.ts` — 'the documented behaviour when the limiter itself is unreachable > is fail-open, and it is a named policy rather than a swallowed error' asserts the constant is "allow". A second copy in the adapter would be one fact stated twice, in a package that cannot import the constant.
declared.what-would-change-it: One constant, in the context, with every use case following and no other edit.
